name: ArtifactAssessment
description: This Resource provides one or more comments, classifiers or ratings about a Resource and supports attribution and rights management metadata for the added content.

element.short: Adds metadata-supported comments, classifiers or ratings related to a Resource
element.definition: This Resource provides one or more comments, classifiers or ratings about a Resource and supports attribution and rights management metadata for the added content.

constraint.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

element.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
element.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resource id depends on the given use case.

element.definition: The metadata about the resource. This is content that is maintained by the infrastructure. Changes to the content might not always be associated with version changes to the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A set of rules under which this content was created
element.definition: A reference to a set of rules that were followed when the resource was constructed, and which must be understood when processing the content. Often, this is a reference to an implementation guide that defines the special rules along with other profiles etc. For DomainResources, if more than one implicitRules policy applies, additional policies may be conveyed using the [additionalImplicitRules](https://build.fhir.org/ig/HL7/fhir-extensions/StructureDefinition-additionalImplicitRules.html) extension.
element.comment: Asserting this rule set restricts the content to be only understood by a limited set of trading partners. This inherently limits the usefulness of the data in the long term. However, the existing health eco-system is highly fractured, and not yet ready to define, collect, and exchange data in a generally computable sense. Wherever possible, implementers and/or specification writers should avoid using this element. Often, when used, the URL is a reference to an implementation guide that defines these special rules as part of its narrative along with other profiles, value sets, etc.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the implicit rules may provide additional knowledge about the resource that modifies its meaning or interpretation

element.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.
element.comment: Language is provided to support indexing and accessibility (typically, services such as text to speech use the language tag). The html language tag in the narrative applies  to the narrative. The language tag on the resource may be used to specify the language of other presentations generated from the data in the resource. Not all the content has to be in the base language. The Resource.language should not be assumed to apply to the narrative automatically. If a language is specified, it should it also be specified on the div element in the html (see rules in HTML5 for information about the relationship between xml:lang and the html lang attribute).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

element.short: Text summary of the resource, for human interpretation
element.definition: A human-readable narrative that contains a summary of the resource and can be used to represent the content of the resource to a human. The narrative need not encode all the structured data, but is required to contain sufficient detail to make it "clinically safe" for a human to just read the narrative. Resource definitions may define what content should be represented in the narrative to ensure clinical safety.
element.comment: Contained resources do not have a narrative. Resources that are not contained SHOULD have a narrative. In some cases, a resource may only have text with little or no additional discrete data (as long as all minOccurs=1 elements are satisfied).  This may be necessary for data from legacy systems where information is captured as a "text blob" or where text is additionally entered raw or narrated and encoded information is added later.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: These resources do not have an independent existence apart from the resource that contains them - they cannot be identified independently, nor can they have their own independent transaction scope. This is allowed to be a Parameters resource if and only if it is referenced by a resource that provides context/meaning.
element.comment: This should never be done when the content can be identified properly, as once identification is lost, it is extremely difficult (and context dependent) to restore it again. Contained resources may have profiles and tags in their meta elements, but SHALL NOT have security labels. Contained resources may be a resource type defined in the FHIR specification, or an [additional resource](resource.html#additional).

element.short: Canonical identifier for this ArtifactAssessment, represented as an absolute URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this ArtifactAssessment when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this ArtifactAssessment is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the ArtifactAssessment is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred. Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author. Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions).

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the ArtifactAssessment to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic
All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Additional identifier for the artifact assessment
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this artifact assessment when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.comment: This may be used for identifiers that can go in an HL7 V3 II (instance identifier) data type, and can then identify this artifact assessment outside of FHIR, where it is not possible to use the logical URI.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the artifact assessment.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the ArtifactAssessment when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the ArtifactAssessment author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a SemVer version, timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd), or incrementing number. There is no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence without additional knowledge.
element.comment: There may be different ArtifactAssessments that have the same canonical url but different versions. The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular canonical version of the ArtifactAssessment with the format [url]|[version]. Note that the canonical version of a resource is not related to a server resource instance version (`Resource.meta.versionId`). For more information, see [Version Matching for Canonical Resources](references.html#matching). The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare canonical versions to determine which is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined. For more information, see [Choosing the right Canonical Reference](references.html#canonical-matching).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: A natural language name identifying the ArtifactAssessment. This name should be usable as an identifier for the resource by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type no-whitespace name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Supports code generation.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: A label for use in displaying and selecting the artifact assessment
element.definition: A label for use in displaying and selecting the artifact assessment.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: The current state of this ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment:
A nominal state-transition diagram can be found in the [Definition pattern](definition.html#statemachine) documentation.

Unknown does not represent 'other' - one of the defined statuses must apply. Unknown is used when the authoring system is not sure what the current status is.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

If a server wishes to reflect whether a given canonical resource is 'supported' or 'enabled' on that server, this is NOT done with status. Instead, expose support for the resource using a 'feature' in the server's CapabilityStatement.
element.requirements: Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content and filtering of ArtifactAssessments that are appropriate for use versus not.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired ArtifactAssessment without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.short: For testing only - never for real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this ArtifactAssessment is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of ArtifactAssessments that are appropriate for use versus not. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource. (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level ArtifactAssessment.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the artifact assessment was published. The date must change when the disposition changes and it must change if the workflow status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the artifact assessment changes.
element.comment: The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the artifact assessment. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the ArtifactAssessment is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the ArtifactAssessment. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the ArtifactAssessment. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context. The publisher is not necessarily an entity that is involved in developing the content of the resource.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the ArtifactAssessment. May also allow for contact.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Natural language description of the ArtifactAssessment
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the ArtifactAssessment from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the ArtifactAssessment as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate ArtifactAssessments.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or even any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the ArtifactAssessment (if applicable)
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating. In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext. The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.comment: It may be possible for the ArtifactAssessment to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.definition: Explanation of why this ArtifactAssessment is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the ArtifactAssessment. Instead, it provides traceability of "why" the resource is either needed or "why" it is defined as it is. This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this ArtifactAssessment.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the artifact assessment and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the artifact assessment.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the artifact assessment and/or its content.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: Describes the clinical usage of the ArtifactAssessment
element.definition: A detailed description of how the ArtifactAssessment is used from a clinical/user perspective.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the artifact assessment was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment: The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the artifact assessment was last reviewed by the publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment: If specified, this date follows the original approval date.
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is. Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.short: When the ArtifactAssessment is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the ArtifactAssessment content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment:
The effective period for a ArtifactAssessment  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a measure intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the ArtifactAssessment are or are expected to be used instead.

constraint.human: All FHIR elements must have a @value or children

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily involved in the development of the content in the ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment: An author does not necessarily have the authority to manage the actual publication of releases of the resource.

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the ArtifactAssessment.

element.definition: An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be primarily responsible for review of some aspect of the ArtifactAssessment.

element.definition: An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be responsible for officially endorsing the ArtifactAssessment for use in some setting.
element.comment: See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.definition: This Resource provides one or more comments, classifiers or ratings about a Resource and supports attribution and rights management metadata for the added content.

constraint.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

element.short: Canonical identifier for this ArtifactAssessment, represented as an absolute URI (globally unique)
element.definition: An absolute URI that is used to identify this ArtifactAssessment when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance; also called its canonical identifier. This SHOULD be globally unique and SHOULD be a literal address at which an authoritative instance of this ArtifactAssessment is (or will be) published. This URL can be the target of a canonical reference. It SHALL remain the same when the ArtifactAssessment is stored on different servers.
element.comment:
Can be a urn:uuid: or a urn:oid: but real http: addresses are preferred. Multiple instances may share the same URL if they have a distinct version.

The determination of when to create a new version of a resource (same url, new version) vs. defining a new artifact is up to the author. Considerations for making this decision are found in [Technical and Business Versions](resource.html#versions).

In some cases, the resource can no longer be found at the stated url, but the url itself cannot change. Implementations can use the [meta.source](resource.html#meta) element to indicate where the current master source of the resource can be found.
element.requirements: Allows the ArtifactAssessment to be referenced by a single globally unique identifier.

constraint.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

element.short: Additional identifier for the artifact assessment
element.definition: A formal identifier that is used to identify this artifact assessment when it is represented in other formats, or referenced in a specification, model, design or an instance.
element.comment: This may be used for identifiers that can go in an HL7 V3 II (instance identifier) data type, and can then identify this artifact assessment outside of FHIR, where it is not possible to use the logical URI.
element.requirements: Allows externally provided and/or usable business identifiers to be easily associated with the artifact assessment.

element.definition: The identifier that is used to identify this version of the ArtifactAssessment when it is referenced in a specification, model, design or instance. This is an arbitrary value managed by the ArtifactAssessment author and is not expected to be globally unique. For example, it might be a SemVer version, timestamp (e.g. yyyymmdd), or incrementing number. There is no expectation that versions can be placed in a lexicographical sequence without additional knowledge.
element.comment: There may be different ArtifactAssessments that have the same canonical url but different versions. The version can be appended to the url in a reference to allow a reference to a particular canonical version of the ArtifactAssessment with the format [url]|[version]. Note that the canonical version of a resource is not related to a server resource instance version (`Resource.meta.versionId`). For more information, see [Version Matching for Canonical Resources](references.html#matching). The version SHOULD NOT contain a '#' - see [Business Version](resource.html#bv-format).

element.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare canonical versions to determine which is more current.
element.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression that has two additional context variables passed in - %version1 and %version2 and will return a negative number if version1 is newer, a positive number if version2 and a 0 if the version ordering can't be successfully be determined. For more information, see [Choosing the right Canonical Reference](references.html#canonical-matching).

element.definition: A natural language name identifying the ArtifactAssessment. This name should be usable as an identifier for the resource by machine processing applications such as code generation.
element.comment: The name is not expected to be globally unique. The name should be a simple alphanumeric type no-whitespace name to ensure that it is machine-processing friendly.
element.requirements: Supports code generation.

element.short: A label for use in displaying and selecting the artifact assessment
element.definition: A label for use in displaying and selecting the artifact assessment.
The current state of this ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment:
A nominal state-transition diagram can be found in the [Definition pattern](definition.html#statemachine) documentation.

Unknown does not represent 'other' - one of the defined statuses must apply. Unknown is used when the authoring system is not sure what the current status is.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

If a server wishes to reflect whether a given canonical resource is 'supported' or 'enabled' on that server, this is NOT done with status. Instead, expose support for the resource using a 'feature' in the server's CapabilityStatement.
element.requirements: Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content and filtering of ArtifactAssessments that are appropriate for use versus not.
element.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired ArtifactAssessment without due consideration

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

element.short: For testing only - never for real usage
element.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this ArtifactAssessment is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
element.comment:
Allows filtering of ArtifactAssessments that are appropriate for use versus not. Experimental resources might include example instances in implementation guides, instances created solely for testing purposes, etc. If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource. (If experimental changes, then it is being misused or a resource that was never intended for real-world use has unexpectedly changed its purpose.).

Experimental resources are not expected to be stable and may well have breaking changes without a corresponding change to the 'version' element.
element.requirements: Enables experimental content to be developed following the same lifecycle that would be used for a production-level ArtifactAssessment.
element.meaningWhenMissing: If absent, this resource is treated as though it is not experimental.

element.definition: The date  (and optionally time) when the artifact assessment was published. The date must change when the disposition changes and it must change if the workflow status code changes. In addition, it should change when the substantive content of the artifact assessment changes.
element.comment: The date is often not tracked until the resource is published, but may be present on draft content. Note that this is not the same as the resource last-modified-date, since the resource may be a secondary representation of the artifact assessment. Additional specific dates may be added as extensions or be found by consulting Provenances associated with past versions of the resource.

element.short: Name of the publisher/steward (organization or individual)
element.definition: The name of the organization or individual responsible for the release and ongoing maintenance of the ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment: Usually an organization but may be an individual. The publisher (or steward) of the ArtifactAssessment is the organization or individual primarily responsible for the maintenance and upkeep of the ArtifactAssessment. This is not necessarily the same individual or organization that developed and initially authored the content. The publisher is the primary point of contact for questions or issues with the ArtifactAssessment. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context. The publisher is not necessarily an entity that is involved in developing the content of the resource.
element.requirements: Helps establish the "authority/credibility" of the ArtifactAssessment. May also allow for contact.

element.definition: Contact details to assist a user in finding and communicating with the publisher.
element.comment:
May be a web site, an email address, a telephone number, etc.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.short: Natural language description of the ArtifactAssessment
element.definition: A free text natural language description of the ArtifactAssessment from a consumer's perspective.
element.comment: This description can be used to capture details such as comments about misuse, instructions for clinical use and interpretation, literature references, examples from the paper world, etc. It is not a rendering of the ArtifactAssessment as conveyed in the 'text' field of the resource itself. This item SHOULD be populated unless the information is available from context.

element.short: The context that the content is intended to support
element.definition: The content was developed with a focus and intent of supporting the contexts that are listed. These contexts may be general categories (gender, age, ...) or may be references to specific programs (insurance plans, studies, ...) and may be used to assist with indexing and searching for appropriate ArtifactAssessments.
element.comment: When multiple useContexts are specified, there is no expectation that all or even any of the contexts apply.
element.requirements: Assist in searching for appropriate content.

element.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the ArtifactAssessment (if applicable)
element.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating. In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext. The useContext may reference additional jurisdictions because the defining jurisdiction does not necessarily limit the jurisdictions of use.
element.comment: It may be possible for the ArtifactAssessment to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

element.definition: Explanation of why this ArtifactAssessment is needed and why it has been designed as it has.
element.comment: This element does not describe the usage of the ArtifactAssessment. Instead, it provides traceability of "why" the resource is either needed or "why" it is defined as it is. This may be used to point to source materials or specifications that drove the structure of this ArtifactAssessment.

element.short: Notice about intellectual property ownership, can include restrictions on use
element.definition: A copyright statement relating to the artifact assessment and/or its contents. Copyright statements are notices of intellectual property ownership and can include restrictions on the use and publishing of the artifact assessment.
element.requirements: Consumers must be able to determine any legal restrictions on the use of the artifact assessment and/or its content.

element.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted. (e.g. 'All rights reserved', 'Some rights reserved').
element.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string. It will be added by software when rendering the notation. Full details about licensing, restrictions, warrantees, etc. goes in the more general 'copyright' element.
element.requirements: Defines the content expected to be rendered in all representations of the artifact.

element.short: Describes the clinical usage of the ArtifactAssessment
element.definition: A detailed description of how the ArtifactAssessment is used from a clinical/user perspective.

element.short: When the artifact assessment was approved by publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was approved by the publisher. Approval happens once when the content is officially approved for usage.
element.comment: The 'date' element may be more recent than the approval date because of minor changes or editorial corrections.

element.short: When the artifact assessment was last reviewed by the publisher
element.definition: The date on which the resource content was last reviewed. Review happens periodically after approval but does not change the original approval date.
element.comment: If specified, this date follows the original approval date.
element.requirements: Gives a sense of how "current" the content is. Resources that have not been reviewed in a long time may have a risk of being less appropriate/relevant.

element.short: When the ArtifactAssessment is expected to be used
element.definition: The period during which the ArtifactAssessment content was or is planned to be in active use.
element.comment:
The effective period for a ArtifactAssessment  determines when the content is applicable for usage and is independent of publication and review dates. For example, a measure intended to be used for the year 2016 might be published in 2015.

See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
element.requirements: Allows establishing a transition before a resource comes into effect and also allows for a sunsetting  process when new versions of the ArtifactAssessment are or are expected to be used instead.

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily involved in the development of the content in the ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment: An author does not necessarily have the authority to manage the actual publication of releases of the resource.

element.definition: An individual or organization primarily responsible for internal coherence of the ArtifactAssessment.
An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be primarily responsible for review of some aspect of the ArtifactAssessment.
element.comment: See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).

element.definition: An individual or organization asserted by the publisher to be responsible for officially endorsing the ArtifactAssessment for use in some setting.
element.comment: See guidance around (not) making local changes to elements [here](canonicalresource.html#localization).
